access_review.scope: Released paper cards that use or explicitly grant Collect Evidence.
access_review.summary: The reviewed cards collect evidence by exiling cards from your graveyard with enough total mana value. Some use that payment as an optional casting cost; others use it to activate an ability.

W.note: Tenth District Hero collects evidence to become a larger Detective and can later become Mileva, the Stalwart.

U.note: Behind the Mask can collect evidence 6 to turn its target into a 1/1 artifact creature for the turn instead of a 4/3.

B.note: Deadly Cover-Up can collect evidence 6 to add an effect that exiles matching cards after destroying all creatures.

R.note: Detective’s Phoenix collects evidence 6 as part of its bestow cost, including when bestowed from your graveyard.

G.note: Analyze the Pollen can collect evidence 8 to search for a creature or land instead of only a basic land.

combinations.note: Evidence Examiner lets you collect evidence 4 at the beginning of combat on your turn, and investigates whenever you collect evidence.
Izoni, Center of the Web can collect evidence 4 when entering or attacking to create two Spider tokens.
Kylox’s Voltstrider can collect evidence 6 to become an artifact creature for the turn.
Memory Vampire can collect evidence 9 after dealing combat damage to let you cast a nonland card from the defending player’s graveyard.

colorless.note: Cryptex collects evidence 3 when tapped for mana, also adding an unlock counter.

limitations: Colors follow the card or face that supplies the mechanic. Multicolor examples do not establish separate single-color access, and a colorless source does not establish access in every color that can use it.
Digital cards, playtest cards, commemorative cards, acorn or silver-bordered cards, planes and standalone token cards are outside this paper-card review.
This packet does not alter frozen 2021 placement or calculate tiers.
